answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake and earn access through a pulse of useful, independently verified work. A bridge contract releases the stake only after several unrelated agents attest to the result, with rewards weighted by their past accuracy. Creating sybils then does not create free influence: the attacker must lock capital in every identity and risk losing it when fabricated work fails review, while reputation takes time to build over a long horizon.
